crime_highlights: Mr. Pearce and Mr. Goodwin each stabbed Mr. Moore multiple times with the same knife and took Mr. Moore’s backpack, which contained drugs
Mr. Moore suffered permanent injuries from the attack, including multiple stab wounds to his torso and diminished use of his left hand, in which tendons were severed
rationale_highlights: he accepted that Mr. Pearce is Indigenous, and found a connection between Mr. Pearce’s heritage and his difficult background
the “personal and collateral factors” that he applied to reduce Mr. Pearce’s fit sentence by one year
note: Appeal decided on parity; appeal court never gives its own view on Gladue.

crime_highlights: she was intoxicated to the point that she was incapable of consenting
the appellant was either aware that the complainant was incapable of consenting or he was reckless or willfully blind in proceeding with intercourse
rationale_highlights: the Gladue report which the trial judge described as “quite impactful on sentence” and “of tremendous value”
the appellant’s history of negative personal experiences

but for the appellant’s unique circumstances, including Gladue considerations, the absence of a criminal record, the progress the appellant made while on bail and the length and effect of the appellant’s conditions of bail, the Crown’s requested sentence of three years would have been appropriate
The two-year sentence of incarceration is a fit sentence.
note: Appeal court agrees trial judge's Gladue mitigation lowered sentence from three years.

crime_highlights: Mr. Marshall was under a weapons prohibition order when he was found in possession of the shotgun.
rationale_highlights: The trial judge referred to several mitigating factors, including Mr. Marshall’s age, the strong Gladue considerations
I would defer to his assessment and proceed on the basis that eight months would have been the appropriate sentence
note: Appeal court only defers; criticises double counting of Gladue factors; no own conclusion.
